decision_conditions: The development hereby permitted shall be carried out in accordance with the following approved plans:Location Plan2104 - Proposed Third Floor Plan2105 - Proposed Roof Plan2112 - Proposed South-West Elevation2113 - Proposed South-East Elevation2111 - Proposed North-West Elevation2110 - Proposed North-East Elevation2115 - Proposed SectionReason: For the avoidance of doubt and in the interests of proper planning.

All new external work shall be carried out in materials that resemble, as closely as possible, in colour and texture those specified in the approved application.Reason: To safeguard the appearance of the premises and the character of the immediate area

Prior to occupation, waste storage and recycling facilities to satisfy the permitted number of occupiers shall be provided on site, in accordance with the Enfield's Household Recycling and Waste Planning Guidance for New Developments (February 2024). Such facilities are to be retained thereafter, unless otherwise agreed in writing by the Local Planning Authority.No existing parking spaces shall be extinguished for the purposes of compliance with this condition.  Reason: To ensure that adequate waste and recycling storage facilities are provided to meet the needs of future occupiers, promote sustainable waste management practices, and support borough-wide recycling targets

Prior to occupation, three long-stay cycle parking spaces shall be provided and  unless otherwise agreed cycle parking should be provided in compliance with the following criteria:o	in an accessible location: the access route to the store should be a minimum of 1.2m wide to enable the bike too	enter the store, should be step free and involve no more than 2 doors or gates (excluding the store door) whicho	must also have a minimum opening width of 1.2mo	secured: with a British Standard mortice lock or access fobo	fully enclosed: 4 walls and a roofThe approved bicycle parking shall be provided prior to occupation and thereafter permanently retained. No existing parking spaces shall be extinguished for the purposes of compliance with this condition. Reason: To ensure that sufficient provision at all times so that the development does not prejudice the free flow of traffic or the conditions of general safety along the adjacent highway, or the amenities and convenience of existing local residents.

No development shall commence until a Flood Risk Access and Egress Verification Scheme has been submitted to and approved in writing by the Local Planning Authority. The scheme shall include:1.	A topographical survey identifying the ground levels at all building points of access/egress and along the primary escape route(s) from the building to an area within Flood Zone 1.2.	Hydraulic Hazard Mapping demonstrating that the primary escape route(s) will maintain a 'Low Hazard' rating (as defined in Table 13.1 of FD2320/TR2) during a 1-in-100 year plus allowance for climate change flood event, accounting for both fluvial and surface water flood risks.3.	A Flood Warning and Evacuation Plan (FWEP), providing evidence of a permanent safe refuge within the new storey and details of the identified 'Low Hazard' escape route to be provided to future occupants.The development shall be carried out in accordance with the approved scheme and the access/egress routes shall be maintained as such thereafterReason: To ensure the safety of future occupants and to minimize the risk to emergency services, in accordance with the NPPF, the Planning Practice Guidance (PPG), and the requirements of Schedule 2, Part 20, Class A of the GPDO, 2015. This information is required prior to commencement because while the host building is situated on higher ground, the surrounding estate is subject to flood risk, and a site-specific 'Low Hazard' route must be verified to satisfy the safety requirements of the Prior Approval process
